company: L1 Global Long Short Fund Limited
title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board, Executives, and the Company Secretary. Subject to trading window restrictions, the absolute hedging ban, and the requirement to obtain the Company's consent before margin lending in respect of Company securities.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board; a subset of Restricted Persons. Additionally must file forms with ASX in respect of their shareholding under section 205G of the Corporations Act and enter into a Director disclosure agreement.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent, or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person. Bound by the same restrictions as apply to the relevant Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 5 trading days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
5 trading days prior to the release of the Company's half-year financial results to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after such release

windows.start_anchor: 5 trading days prior to the release of the Company's full-year financial results to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after such release

windows.start_anchor: 5 trading days prior to the Company's Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further periods of time as a prohibited period, and the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties trading at any time; confidentiality of such embargoes is not addressed.

rules.detail: The policy contains no definition of 'dealing' or 'securities' that expressly sweeps in third-party derivatives. An OTC put or call over the Company's shares operates to limit the economic risk of holding those shares, so it is caught by the absolute hedging prohibition, which has no clearance or exceptional-circumstances carve-out.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on hedging arrangements over Company securities (shares, options and rights), applying to Restricted Persons and, via section 5.3, their Associated Parties. No vesting-state distinction and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure that limits the economic risk of holding the shares would be a hedging arrangement within the section 5.10 definition and is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in this extract of the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in this extract of the policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing the Company's shares used to offset a shareholding's economic exposure would be a hedging arrangement and is banned; a CFD taken without an underlying holding is not otherwise addressed.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Margin lending using Company securities (or transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, or selling to satisfy a margin call) is prohibited without the Company's prior consent; the Company may make any clearance conditional on terms it sees fit. Applies to Restricted Persons and, via 5.3, Associated Parties.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: Only encumbrance in the specific form of a margin lending arrangement is addressed, requiring the Company's prior consent; a charge or lien securing a loan not structured as a conventional 'margin lending arrangement' is not clearly covered by this wording.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: The policy addresses only 'margin lending arrangements', not secured financing generally. Whether a bespoke bank loan secured against the collared shares (not structured or labelled as a conventional margin loan) falls within 'or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement' is untested; if it does, Company consent (potentially conditional) is required and can be withheld or conditioned at the Company's discretion.
rules.evidence: or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, buy/sell window or short-term/speculative trading restriction is stated in this extract of the policy.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, in conference with the Chairperson
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's shares, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings. This should be done by written notice to the Company Secretary ... The Company Secretary will confer with the Chairperson in relation to any proposed dealing.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: not specified in this extract (per s205G Corporations Act and the Listing Rules)
clearance.evidence: The Directors are required to complete, or request that the Company Secretary complete, necessary forms to be filed with ASX in respect of their shareholding in the Company for the purposes of section 205G of the Corporations Act and the Listing Rules.

exceptions.approver: Chairperson (or another Director if the Chairperson is the person requesting clearance)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship ... clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell shares in the Company
other circumstances that may be deemed exceptional by the Chairperson.
undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of shares in lieu of a cash dividend)
the sale of sufficient entitlements to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act
the purchase of shares or the communication of information pursuant to a requirement imposed by law
bona fide gifts to a Director by a third party
transfers of shares in the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme that invests in securities of the Company (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of the Company by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Shareholders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

external_documents: Insider Trading Policy (Corporate Governance Charter, section 6) - referenced but not included in this extract
exemption_authority: The Chairperson may grant clearance for a sale only (not a purchase) in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or enforceable undertaking, another overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or other circumstances the Chairperson deems exceptional), but not while there is a matter about which there is inside information; where the Chairperson is the person seeking clearance, another Director decides.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even under the hardship exception, only a sale can be cleared during a blackout, so unwinding a written call position (which may require a purchase) could not rely on this exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 5.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regard to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate or veto the bank's forced-sale/margin-call mechanics as a condition of clearing the loan leg of a funded collar, giving it effective control over the facility's enforcement terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Share Trading Policy ... applies to ... the Board; Executives; and the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy has no vesting, holding-lock or minimum shareholding provisions, indicating the target holders' shares are ordinary market-acquired holdings rather than unvested equity incentives, simplifying the security-state analysis for a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her "associated parties" ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or company does not avoid the hedging ban or the margin loan consent requirement.

bespoke_clauses.topic: insider trading policy incorporated by reference
bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition to the requirements of this Share Trading Policy, all Restricted Persons (as defined below) must also comply with the Insider Trading Policy in section 6 below.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 6 (not included in this document) may contain a broader 'dealing' definition that more clearly addresses OTC derivatives; it should be obtained and reviewed before relying on this analysis.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy as extracted. Section 5.10 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on hedging arrangements over Company securities, defined broadly as financial products that limit the economic risk of holding the shares, with no clearance route or exceptional-circumstances carve-out, so both the purchased put and written call legs are prohibited outright. Margin lending is treated differently and more favourably: section 5.11 permits margin lending, transfers into a margin account, and margin-call sales with the Company's prior consent, which the Company may make conditional on terms of its choosing (including forced-sale mechanics), but this provision is framed around conventional 'margin lending arrangements' and it is untested whether a bespoke bank loan secured against collared shares would qualify. Even if the loan leg could be structured to fit within section 5.11, the hedging ban makes the collar's derivative legs impossible without an amendment to or waiver of the policy, and the sale-only exceptional-circumstances clearance in section 5.8 would not obviously assist. Trading (and presumably any collar-related dealing) is also barred during four recurring blackout windows and any ad hoc embargo the Board imposes at its absolute discretion.
